chunks: And from that is the saying of the Truthful One (peace be upon him):

Nothing appeared to Allah as an appearance (change in knowledge/apparent decree) as it appeared to Him regarding my son Isma'il. He says: No matter became apparent to Allah as it became apparent to Him regarding my son Isma'il, when He cut him off [by death] before me, so that it may be known by that that he was not the Imam after me.

key_terms.بَدَاء: Al-Bada' (the appearing or manifesting of something to God that was previously hidden or apparent in decree)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about Isma'il and the concept of Al-Bada'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs the doctrine of Al-Bada' to clarify the temporary nature of Isma'il's imamate, explaining that Allah's apparent decree regarding his son's death was a divine sign to distinguish him from the permanent successor. This narration underscores the Shia belief that leadership succession is not always linear or predetermined in a fixed manner, but can be adjusted by divine will to ensure the correct Imam is identified. The event serves as a theological proof for the fluidity of divine decree in matters of guidance, reinforcing the authority of the Imams to interpret such signs.
